question: How many isosceles triangles are there with positive area whose side lengths are all positive integers and whose longest side has length \(2025?\)
solution:
Separate the triangles according to whether the longest side occurs at least twice or exactly once.

If at least two sides have length \(2025\), the side lengths are
\[
(2025,2025,k),\qquad 1\le k\le2025.
\]
Every such integer \(k\) gives a positive-area triangle: \(2025+k>2025\) and \(2025+2025>k\). This gives \(2025\) triangles, including the equilateral triangle.

If exactly one side has length \(2025\), the other two sides must be equal. Write the lengths as \((k,k,2025)\), where \(k<2025\). The triangle inequality requires
\[
2k>2025.
\]
Hence the possible integers are \(1013\) through \(2024\), giving
\[
2024-1013+1=1012
\]
triangles.

The cases cover all possibilities and do not overlap. Within either case, different values of \(k\) give different side lengths. Therefore the total is
\[
2025+1012=\boxed{3037}.
\]
The answer is choice \(\text{D}\).
